name: episode_create
title: Create an episode or derived reel
description: Assembles a new EPISODE or derived reel from ordered recording/episode/template ranges into ONE combined video. A reel cut from an Episode takes derived_from_id for lineage and one segment row per chosen moment in the canonical shape {episode_id, range:[start_seconds,end_seconds]}; segments[].range is a half-open [start,end) interval in EPISODE time. derived_from_id does not select a range. Creation selects Program ranges; simultaneous participant boxes are composed afterwards with camera_program_set, not with extra segment fields. Use this when the user asks to make, cut together, or export a multi-segment highlight, reel, montage, or supercut. Suggestions alone create nothing (saved Moments are review_points_place), and a single-range Clip is clip_create. Branding: identity:"project_default" applies the project's saved Signature defaults (the user's branding); identity_assets_list lists the saved assets an explicit choice names. Episode-range slices keep what their parent plays there (a pinned or replaced microphone, silence) and program_audio names it; audio that cannot be carried, such as a pinned microphone in a montage without derived_from_id, refuses with program_audio_not_preservable and its exact span. Persists the edit only — does not render or charge. The rendered video is a separate render_create with the exact returned target_type, target_id, and revision; render_status reports it. Publishing is separate. Always returns edge_warnings. A warning means a cut edge overlaps an approximate transcript word span, not that acoustic evidence proved a mid-word cut. Each warning's episode_seconds is the created target's point for a narrow episode_zoom region and edge, and occurrence_id and source_id identify the exact side; when those coordinates are absent, episode_read of the target maps the edge. A point whose speech evidence is supported inter_word_silence or supported aligned_word_edge stands; any other point is revised on the same target with episode_edit at an exact supported point. Acoustic envelope/onset suggestions alone are not boundary authority. A second episode_create or a superseding Clip does not resolve edge_warnings. Accepts idempotency_key. A creation with derived_from_id produces a Clip (a derived Episode IS a Clip), addressed as target_type:"clip" in render_create, render_status, and workspace_open. A canvas taller than the source picture (a portrait canvas over landscape footage) keeps only a vertical slice of each frame; episode_framing_guidance reports, per visible person, whether their measured extent fits that crop window (fits | too_wide | uncertain | unknown), and episode_edit occurrence.reframe carries the framing decision.

segments.description: Ordered episode/recording/template segments. The only model-visible boundary field is range: {episode_id, range:[start,end]} in EPISODE time or {recording_id, range:[start,end]} in SOURCE time, both half-open [start,end) intervals; episode_range and start_seconds/end_seconds are not accepted. Template rows use {template, params} and have no range.

episode_id.description: Source Episode public ID. This row must also provide range in half-open EPISODE time.

recording_id.description: Source Recording public ID. This row must also provide range in half-open SOURCE time.

template.description: Curated block template key, such as show_open/studio_dissolve or outro/sting_chime.

range.description: Required for episode_id and recording_id rows. The field is named range and contains the half-open interval [start_seconds, end_seconds): EPISODE time for episode_id, SOURCE time for recording_id.

boundary_rationale.description: Optional audit notes for selected boundaries.

zoom_regions.description: Optional audit list of consulted source/episode windows.

derived_from_id.description: Optional parent Episode public ID used only for lineage/filing. It does not select media or replace segments[].range. It files a multi-segment reel cut from one existing Episode under that parent instead of listing it as a primary project Episode.

aspect_ratio.description: Output shape, set only for a shape the user asked for or a named vertical destination (Reels/Shorts/TikTok). When omitted it follows the footage: the source recording's native aspect, nearest of 9:16/16:9/1:1, and 16:9 when unprobed. "Reel" describes the edit, not the shape: 9:16 on landscape footage crops the sides away and can cut a second person out of frame.

transition.description: Optional seam transition for segment boundaries. Defaults to cut.

opener.description: Explicit opener library_entry_id returned by identity_assets_list, or none; a specific saved asset instead of project_default.

outro.description: Explicit outro library_entry_id returned by identity_assets_list, or none; a specific saved asset instead of project_default.

identity.description: Optional highlight-reel Signature. project_default applies the project's saved Signature defaults (the user's branding); saved project music becomes a full-Episode music cue. identity_assets_list lists saved openers and outros with their uses_title. The object form chooses explicit saved opener and outro assets. A specific song is added or changed with music_cue_mutate after creation. Omitted object keys mean none.

opener_title.description: Optional per-reel opener title, used only when the selected opener asset has uses_title:true; static or absent openers return identity_warnings:["opener_title_ignored_static_opener"] and ignore this value.

supersedes_episode_id.description: Optional explicit lineage for a replacement draft the user deliberately asks for. It does not resolve edge_warnings, which are revised on the same created target with episode_edit.

idempotency_key.description: Opaque key unique across the account for this logical creation. Under a v3 editor ask it is the full requestId plus a distinct action suffix; otherwise it is a fresh opaque key chosen once. Exact retry/recovery reuses the original complete key and arguments, including across later messages. A key derived from titles or media ranges changes with them, and a new key on an ambiguous write can create a duplicate. A near-duplicate this same session already created comes back with near_duplicate:true instead of a second row.

examples.label: Create a top-level episode from recording ranges
Create a derived highlight reel under one parent episode
Create a top-level montage from multiple episodes

near_duplicate.description: True when nothing was created because this session already made a near-identical derived clip; the returned handles are that existing clip's. That clip is refined with episode_edit; repeating the create returns it again.

already_applied.description: True when the returned persisted Clip was already in place: either an exact same-key replay, or (with near_duplicate:true) same-session range convergence.

clip_id.description: Present when target_type is clip. The episode_id alias remains for compatibility.

target_type.description: Structural kind of the created composition.

target_id.description: Canonical handle for the created Episode or Clip.

title.description: Persisted title of the created Episode or Clip.

segment_count.description: Number of persisted Program segments in the returned target.

creation_disposition.description: Whether this call created a target, replayed the exact idempotent create, or converged onto an existing near-duplicate.

total_duration_seconds.description: Total Program duration, including applied identity segments.

content_duration_seconds.description: Duration of the requested editorial content before identity additions.

derived_from_id.description: Parent Episode handle when the created target is a Clip.

identity_opener.description: Compact applied opener summary when present.

workspace_url.description: BitterClip workspace URL for the created target.

revision.description: Durable revision counter (starts at 1 for a fresh episode).

tool_outcome.description: Persisted production receipt with the exact target, revision, and next Open action.

segments.description: The persisted segment manifest (index, source_id, source_label, source_range, episode_range, boundary).

block_segments.description: Template-backed segments created during this request.

status.description: Whether the template-backed Recording is already renderable or still baking.

edge_warnings.description: Always present. Non-mutating flags for cut edges that overlap approximate transcript word spans; acoustic verification decides whether the existing point is supported.

at_seconds.description: Recording source time for the flagged edge. This legacy field name is not Episode time.

source_id.description: Recording containing the flagged source edge.

occurrence_id.description: Exact created-target occurrence containing this edge, when mapped.

episode_seconds.description: Exact flagged point on the created target's Episode clock, usable directly as an episode_zoom edge; occurrence_id identifies its source side.

identity_plan.description: Frozen resolved identity plan when identity: project_default resolved to an applied project identity.

identity_layers.description: Resolved Signature layers such as opener, cut style, and outro.

identity_segments.description: Identity-inserted segment rows with role, final_position, and segment_id for follow-up edits.

identity_warnings.description: Identity warnings such as project_identity_missing or unsupported identity config.

request_row_map.description: Mapping from requested rows to final composition positions, including segment_id. Identity insertion shifts these positions.

derived.description: True when this edit is filed under a parent episode via derived_from_id and hidden from the primary episode index.

derived_episode.description: Present and true only for a top-level montage assembled from episode_id segments without derived_from_id.

derived_from_episode_ids.description: Source episode IDs used to assemble a top-level montage episode.

program_audio.description: Present on a fresh create cut from existing Episodes/Clips: preserved is true because each selected range was proven to play the same Recording and source second (or silence) as its parent. settled says how: none (plain occurrence audio), pin, intervals or pin_and_intervals.

pinned_camera_group_key.description: The camera group the new target's Program audio is pinned to, when settled includes pin.

authorities.description: Seconds of the new target played by each authority and Recording.

status.description: Always draft — persisted but not rendered.
